supporting_news.title: India bonds give up marginal opening gains as profit booking takes over
supporting_news.summary: On Monday, Indian government bonds experienced a decline following an initial gain earlier in the day. Traders engaged in profit booking, particularly after last week's significant trends in the market. The Indian rupee sharply fell towards the 93 per US dollar mark, impacting investor sentiment. Additionally, investors are focusing on the Reserve Bank of India's policy decision scheduled for December 4.

supporting_news.title: India’s rupee has become an accidental carry star
supporting_news.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has made moves that temporarily attract carry traders to the rupee. Recent factors include decreasing oil prices and a shift in foreign investment from artificial intelligence stocks to Indian markets. However, these RBI incentives may not last, leaving uncertainty for traders. India's interest rate advantage has significantly diminished since 2011, raising concerns. Policymakers face challenges in ensuring sustained interest in the rupee amid historical depreciation.

supporting_news.title: India bonds give up marginal opening gains as profit booking takes over
supporting_news.summary: Indian government bonds fell after initial gains due to profit booking by traders and a sharp rupee decline. The benchmark yield of the 6.94% 2036 bond increased to 7.2185% during trading hours. Last week, the yield had dropped significantly due to lower US Treasury yields and a stronger rupee. Investors now focus on the upcoming Reserve Bank of India's policy decision on December 4.

supporting_news.title: Shift in pension and insurance money to equities dampens long-term G-sec demand: RBI DG
supporting_news.summary: The demand for long-term government securities has seen a marginal decline recently. Insurance companies and pension funds are increasingly focusing on equities instead of sovereign debt. This change has impacted the stability of the government securities market and highlighted challenges in liquidity distribution. The Reserve Bank of India emphasizes the need for a coordinated approach and broader participation from institutional investors.

supporting_news.title: A 50 bps jumbo rate hike can lead to financial stability concerns, hurt growth: Report
supporting_news.summary: SBI economists have lowered their rate hike expectations for the upcoming RBI policy review. They now anticipate a 0.25 per cent increase rather than the previously expected 0.50 per cent. This adjustment stems from concerns regarding financial stability and potential impacts on economic growth. The RBI's monetary policy committee is scheduled to meet from December 2 to December 4.
